page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-32 is a compute-focused instance within the cost-optimized E2 family. It is provisioned with 32 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:1 ratio of 1.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The compute allocation is backed by dedicated AMD EPYC 7B12 processors running on the x86_64 architecture, configured as 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with instruction support for AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI.

Hardware accelerators and integrated storage are omitted on this profile; the instance contains 0 GPUs and includes no local storage (storage is 'None'). Benchmark results place single-core CPU throughput in the upper 25% bracket, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 2690.17. Multi-threaded processing reaches middle-tier levels across synthetic workloads, with a stress-ng multi-core metric of 43150.61, a PassMark CPU score of 38354.69, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11360.0. Memory bandwidth measures 82.87 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 51.96 GB/sec for large-block writes.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances high thread counts against lower memory density to deliver cost-efficient compute capacity. While raw single-core execution is competitive, lack of embedded NVMe disks and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 limits applicability in vector-heavy mathematics or disk-bound data pipelines. Consequently, the configuration is best matched for compute-bound tasks that do not demand extensive RAM pools, such as CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch processing jobs, microservices hosting, and horizontal web serving tiers.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-32 is a compute-skewed virtual machine featuring 32 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, backed by an AMD EPYC 7B12 x86_64 processor across 16 physical cores. Offering a 1:1 vCPU-to-memory allocation, it does not include bundled local storage or GPUs. Stress-ng single-core performance registers in the top 25% with a score of 2690.17, while multi-core compute tests such as Geekbench (11360.0) and PassMark CPU (38354.69) place the instance within average industry brackets. Memory throughput achieves 82.87 GB/sec for large read operations. The hardware balance provides reliable, cost-efficient thread density for workloads that favor parallel processing over high memory capacity, making it a fit for CI/CD compilation, batch workloads, web serving, and parallel integer processing.
